DJIA

The DJIA was created to measure the movements of the leading companies in the United States engaged in industrial activities. It uses the price-weighted index, meaning that stocks with a high share price carry a greater weight in the index than stocks with a low share price.

  • $ gainers/losers is based on $ change value

Nasdaq 100

The Nasdaq 100 includes the stocks of the 100 largest, non-financial companies listed on Nasdaq. The Nasdaq 100 is calculated by the market capitalization of its constituents. The 100 companies in the Nasdaq 100 make up more than 90% of the weight of the Nasdaq Composite Index.

S&P 500

The S&P 500 features 500 leading U.S. publicly traded companies, with a primary emphasis on market capitalization. The S&P 500 is a float-weighted index, meaning the market capitalizations of the companies in the index are adjusted by the number of shares available for public trading.
